NCSA Mosaic (web browser)

The 1993 browser that brought pages with inline images, blue underlined links, and a gray page ground to a wide audience.

Source
Wikimedia Commons: NCSA Mosaic Browser Screenshot
Creator
National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA), University of Illinois
Made
1993 (browser); 2013 (screenshot by Charles Severance)
Style
Brutalist web design (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Plain, utilitarian
Evidence
The Commons screenshot (772 × 668 px, CC0, by Charles Severance, 2013) is below the 800 px threshold for an observed record, so no traits are recorded as observed. The release year comes from general histories and was not checked against an NCSA source.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

This is a lineage reference. Mosaic’s default page ground was gray, not white.

Context

The Commons description reads “NCSA Mosaic for X Screenshot”. The license is CC0 for the screenshot, but the browser interface belongs to the University of Illinois, so the image is not stored.

NN/g (2017) ties the style to early 1990s websites, which were shaped by browsers of this generation.

Why it belongs

A source for the defaults that Brutalist web design restates: link blue, underlines, bold serif headings, and native gray controls. A larger image is needed to record the traits as observed.
